subject: Urgent: post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike affecting MarqueePay
messages:
-- Message 1 --
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@marqueepay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: MarqueePay SRE <sre@marqueepay.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@marqueepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike (started ~07:50 UTC)

Hi Marcus / Monica,

We rolled the V3.1 model + new quantization profile into production for our MarqueePay integration at 07:45 UTC. Since ~07:50 UTC we are seeing a sustained p99 latency increase (from ~210ms to ~1.1s) and a jump in 500/502 errors for the tokenization/generation path. This is impacting transaction enrichment calls and causing timeouts upstream.

I attached a perf snapshot and a short error trace. Our SRE team is concerned about tail latency and memory pressure on the pods. Can Redwood confirm whether any kernel/seq-len-based fallback logic changed with the V3.1 quant profile?

We need an immediate mitigation plan; at minimum we need to avoid user-visible timeouts.

Thanks,
Alex
Sr. Platform Engineer
MarqueePay
[Attachment: perf_snapshot_20260820.csv] [Attachment: error_trace_20260820.log]

-- Message 2 --
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@marqueepay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike (started ~07:50 UTC)

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the traces. Monica and I are triaging now. Initial read: the V3.1 release introduced a new quant profile that alters kernel selection heuristics for short-context requests; that could explain higher CPU scheduling on the inference nodes.

Immediate plan:
- Monica: confirm whether MarqueePay is routed to the new V3.1 pool or a fallback variant.
- Aditya (eng): can you look at the kernel/queue metrics and whether spinning up additional inference replicas or reverting quant profile is safer?

We’ll update within 30 minutes with either a mitigation (scale/route) or a rollback ETA. Sorry for the disruption.

– Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

-- Message 3 --
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@marqueepay.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: MarqueePay SRE <sre@marqueepay.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@marqueepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike (started ~07:50 UTC)

Quick update — MarqueePay is indeed on the V3.1 quant profile pool (tag: q-v3.1). Routing shows ~92% of requests hitting the V3.1 variant; ~8% are hitting v3.0 fallback by policy.

Observations from our dashboard (07:40–09:10 UTC window):
- p99 latency: 210ms -> 1.1s (V3.1), p50/p90 less affected
- 5xx rate: 0.02% -> 1.8% concentrated on generation shard 4
- CPU steal and kernel time higher on nodes hosting q-v3.1 replicas

I’m attaching the perf snapshot. I recommend either:
A) Immediate traffic split rollback to v3.0 (route 100% to v3.0) — fastest to restore SLAs
B) Temporary scale-up of q-v3.1 replicas (adds capacity but slower to observe)

Which should we do?

— Monica
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: perf_snapshot_20260820.csv]

-- Message 4 --
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@marqueepay.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@marqueepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike (started ~07:50 UTC) — Executive sync

Looping in leadership for visibility. Alex — apologies for the impact. Marcus, Monica, Aditya: please propose a clear mitigation and a short-lived rollback plan we can approve. We need:
- Customer-facing ETA to restore normal p99 (15–30 min target)
- Root-cause hypothesis (one paragraph)
- Risks of rollback (data/consistency/throughput)

I expect an update in 30 minutes; if we can restore within 30m we will not escalate to broader exec.

— Evelyn
Director, Customer Success Operations

-- Message 5 --
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@marqueepay.com>, MarqueePay SRE <sre@marqueepay.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-upgrade latency & 5xx spike (started ~07:50 UTC) — Mitigation and rollback plan

Team — follow-up after debugging overnight. Summary:
- Root cause (short): the V3.1 quant profile introduced a codepath that prefers a GPU kernel optimized for longer context; for short inputs this forces an unnecessary fallback that increases memory shuffles and causes higher kernel queueing on nodes with mixed batch sizes. That produced the p99 spike and localized 5xx due to OOM-retry cycles on shard 4.
- What we did: 2026-08-20 10:20 UTC we switched MarqueePay to 100% v3.0 (routing rollback) — p99 returned to ~230ms within 8 minutes and 5xx dropped to baseline.
- Proposed persistent fix: revert the q-v3.1 heuristic for short-context routing and publish q-v3.1.1 with a guarded rollout and additional perf tests.
- Rollback risks: minimal customer data risk; only runtime variant routing changed. Throughput briefly dropped during the cutover (~3% for ~5m) but SLAs met.

Attachments: rollback_plan_v1.md (detailed steps), perf snapshot post-rollback.

Next steps assigned:
- Aditya: implement guarded q-v3.1.1 and add kernel selection unit tests (ETA 5 business days)
- Marcus: coordinate customer post-mortem and offer one-time credit for SLA impact (if requested)
- Monica: confirm closure with MarqueePay and attach remediation notes in HubSpot record

Alex / Priya — sorry again for the disruption. Let us know if you want a joint incident review next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime
[Attachment: rollback_plan_v1.md]
